# Authenticated one-shot authored codec: complete small FRAME candidate

This is an isolated, noninstallable experiment. It changes no product source,
service, database, package, or user collection. The old standalone archive is
unchanged. Do not use its historical producer entry points as deployment tools.

Run from a clean checkout with the existing Node/jsdom development dependency:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_experimental_authored_codec_frame.py' -v
```

The only source card is **real 2026 `abolish`**, canonical ID
`f874ff4280b56e0b301f6c9275298a138ab990ec815d81d75225a87ae1c519bc`.
The original source wrapper is 65,595 bytes, SHA
`34b5a2498d23b379adc2ac0ff17b448059acd59030f9e6a5590e24ae271761a0`;
the complete original prepared artifact is 225,518 bytes, SHA
`a6d88ed5971734e4366cfb71b3077a2f4e938b6bc03de24218738e3edb58ddf8`.
No profile from a different book/cohort was substituted. One bounded original
small producer invocation completed in 1.37 seconds; its baseline and captured
results have identical final panels, examples, and native statistics. Those are
historical generation observations, not browser timings. The existing bank
rejections (four source-anchor-count cases) are preserved, not silently fixed.
The test does not rerun that producer or any large-card producer.
The external compiled runtime is the original approved `e56d2656…37bc`;
the existing frozen-profile adaptation still runs at its original verified hook.
The native module stays original `5c361607…a15e` / prepared `7f16cca5…95b4`.

`generate.cjs` uses the sealed small canonical capture/export. It runs the exact
original first codec only after validating original policy entries, actual full
resource SHA bytes, inline bytes/SHA, and the entire approved 14-pin order. It
never infers identity from filenames. Unsupported/missing/reordered/duplicate
cohorts keep the original HTML bytes, with no generation codec execution. The
final post-codec DOM supplies the binding paths and required attributes. This
real card is already idempotently decoded, so generation makes zero HTML edits.

`frame.cjs` makes twelve exact reversible edits to the existing complete
resource-proof + frozen-profile FRAME candidate (baseline `052ccc54…afa59d`):

1. Substitute this small externally pinned asset descriptor.
2. Keep a private WeakMap of the exact successful `support.load` result identity
   and original packet/side/token validation closure. No self-attested boolean
   can certify another object.
3. Reuse that **same** authenticated, parsed and recursively frozen profile and
   the already parsed inert HTML; add no profile SHA, JSON parse, DOM parse, or
   deep-freeze. Register immediately before synchronous original node adoption.
4. Around the first actual 9014 execution, install a temporary private capability
   guard before the existing v5 adapter. The one-shot proof retires permanently
   after acceptance or relevant drift/cancel; the second execution follows the
   original path. Dispose on old-document replacement/cleanup.

The original collector's source policy, SHA checks, order and native-module
reuse stay active. All 15 actual original script lexemes (14 executable source
positions and one JSON payload) are exact. The remaining four IIFEs of both
9014 invocations remain byte-identical. The original source-side checks,
source-resource validation, native readiness, font, child and stable-geometry
commit gates are not changed. `inverse.test.cjs` proves exact inverses of the
FRAME edits, helper extraction, profile-projector adaptation and author guard.
The frozen reconstructed FRAME includes existing diagnostic helper definitions;
this test enables no QA clock/metrics asset and makes no performance claim.

Observed by the complete FRAME fixture:

- The actual 12 nonmodule source author invocations execute in original order,
  including both complete 9014 authors; two native-module source positions reuse
  the authenticated module definition as in the original FRAME.
- The native payload reaches `ready`, complete front/back mount succeeds, and
  both 9014 invocations together reduce static codec discovery from **6 to 3**.
  The first invocation skips its three searches; the second retains all three.
- Original sentences/translations, chunks, four audit-reason notes and Find-visible
  closed content match the original full FRAME. Reader/chunk/year controls and
  prepared flips remain functional; flips do not rerun source authors.
- Wrong source/derived bytes fail closed, unsupported certificates and DOM drift
  use the original codec, and cancelled pending loads cannot revive an ABA owner.
- Unmeasured/stale child events and loading fonts block submission. The real
  gate processes simulated well-formed/stale messages; **JSDOM has no physical
  child layout measurement**. Browser, largest-card, cross-device and performance
  acceptance are separate remaining work. This real small card has no nonempty
  ownership-history subgroup; it does not stand in for that large-card variant. No instant-speed claim is made. The JSDOM harness fixes only its child
  `Date.now` to compare the original live countdown deterministically; the
  uninstrumented candidate does not contain that test clock.

`*.gz` files are deterministic, lossless fixture storage only. Tests read bounded
local data and make no network requests. `producer-*` files preserve the original
historical once-only generation provenance; they are never executed by tests.
The existing sibling compiled-card/standalone fixtures are pin-checked references,
not ignored-output dependencies. `FROZEN.json` seals this complete sibling archive;
the root agent receives its external SHA for independent review.
